skills.name: Essay planning, thesis statements and topic sentences

note.text: An essay needs a focus and an order that helps the reader. A thesis statement presents the controlling idea or position; a topic sentence gives the main idea of a paragraph. Supporting details explain, illustrate or qualify that idea. A plan is an outline, not the final essay. An introduction should prepare the reader for the focus, while a conclusion draws together the developed ideas. Avoid claiming that every essay type needs an identical rigid formula.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to plan a focused essay with a controlling idea and paragraphs that develop it. Builds on: directed-writing purpose and sentence accuracy. Leads to: argumentative and narrative writing with an organised structure.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: An essay needs a focus and an order that helps the reader. A thesis statement presents the controlling idea or position; a topic sentence gives the main idea of a paragraph. Supporting details explain, illustrate or qualify that idea. A plan is an outline, not the final essay. An introduction should prepare the reader for the focus, while a conclusion draws together the developed ideas. Avoid claiming that every essay type needs an identical rigid formula.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Original plan on reading clubs: Focus: a club can support reading when members participate. Paragraph idea: shared discussion clarifies understanding. Support: members compare reasons for an interpretation. Paragraph idea: organisation makes participation possible. Support: clear roles and suitable meeting times. Ending: the club’s value depends on active use. A sample topic sentence is Shared discussion helps members test their understanding.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: State one manageable focus. Group related points and give each paragraph a clear role. Check that evidence supports the paragraph idea and that the paragraph serves the overall focus. Do not confuse a paragraph’s opening sentence with the whole essay’s thesis.

paper_task.prompt: Plan an essay on how a school club can help learners. Write a controlling statement, paragraph ideas with support and a proposed conclusion. Develop one planned paragraph into prose.

Support: members compare reasons for an interpretation. Paragraph idea: organisation makes participation possible. Support: clear roles and suitable meeting times. Ending: the club’s value depends on active use. A sample topic sentence is Shared discussion helps members test their understanding.
checklist: My focus is clear and manageable.
Each planned paragraph has relevant support.
My developed paragraph follows its topic sentence.
